items.question: Why does old iron not rust?
items.pov_line: Failure isn't an insult to engineering; pretending failure has been eliminated is. Every material has conditions, limits and a life. The question is whether those limits were understood and monitored, or ignored until the failure became somebody else's emergency.
items.pov_bank_line: Failure isn't an insult to engineering; pretending failure has been eliminated is. Every material has conditions, limits and a life. The question is whether those limits were understood and monitored, or ignored until the failure became somebody else's emergency.
items.pov_script_line: I wanted a clean number for how long a protective layer takes to form. The published corrosion rates span two orders of magnitude, so a single figure would have sounded more certain than the evidence actually is.

items.question: How is a silicon wafer made?
items.pov_line: Watching something be made, I think about how many things had to become controllable first — temperature, pressure, purity, timing, tolerances, sequence, inspection. What looks smooth at the end is usually violent forces being controlled very precisely.
items.pov_bank_line: Watching something be made, I think about how many things had to become controllable first — temperature, pressure, purity, timing, tolerances, sequence, inspection. What looks smooth at the end is usually violent forces being controlled very precisely.
items.pov_script_line: I wrote 'nine-nines pure' like purity was a certificate stamped once. It isn't. Every step after purification can reintroduce contamination, so I rewrote it as a chain of measurements instead of an achieved state.
sources_cited: MIT Department of Materials Science and Engineering

items.question: What is a semiconductor made of?
items.pov_line: It reminds me of companies and systems. Something looks completely irrational when you judge it outside the environment it was built for.
items.pov_bank_line: It reminds me of companies and systems. Something looks completely irrational when you judge it outside the environment it was built for.
items.pov_script_line: 'What is it made of' sounds like it wants one element. Silicon is over ninety percent of production, but the defining property is the impurity deliberately added to it, not the base material. I answered the question underneath the question.

items.question: How is 3D printed metal made?
items.pov_line: A remarkable laboratory property is not the same thing as a reliable system.
items.pov_bank_line: A remarkable laboratory property is not the same thing as a reliable system.
items.pov_script_line: I wanted to say the layers get welded together, because that's the intuitive word. They don't weld, they fuse metallurgically — the atoms interdiffuse across the boundary. Wrong verb, wrong physics, so I cut it.
